correctness.rationale: The Newton identities identify the three generators with a regular subsequence of polynomial symmetric invariants. Invertibility of a 3-column Vandermonde determinant shows singular coordinates assume at most two values. Multiplicity equations with p<n<2p force exactly p equal nonzero and r zero coordinates; no other geometric values are allowed. At every such point the tangent-constrained quadratic form has Gram blocks I+J with determinants -1 and r mod p, so is nondegenerate: formal Morse lemma gives an ordinary node and reduced Jacobian point. CM and codimension >=2 singular support yield normality, and projective CI connectedness yields geometric integrality. Exact modular checks and exhaustive P^5(F5) census passed; only uniform proof establishes all extension-field cases.

The all-primes classification addresses p<n<2p where the main published singular-dimension/normality theorem does not apply, giving an explicit complete reduced singular scheme, exact count, local analytic type and a natural six-node K3 surface at p=5.
